raw_response:
I will run the year around one clear priority: I will keep stevia as my main cash crop and use the rest of the land for a simple wheat-summer maize rotation. I have only 6 mu and a two-person household, so I will not spread myself too thin or chase complicated management. In Quzhou, stevia already has a local purchase and service chain, and local reports show it can return much more than ordinary grain, so I will put 4 mu into stevia and manage it carefully with timely irrigation, weed control, and moderate fertilizer. I will keep 2 mu in winter wheat followed by summer maize because I have 50 years of experience with grain, I have well irrigation, and grain gives me stability. I will use improved or hybrid materials, keep tillage simple, avoid excessive nitrogen, and rely on a few timely irrigations instead of rough, heavy input use.
